name: Venus
blurb: Magellan and Pioneer Venus gravity (SHGJ180U). A topography grid can be added with Load planet.

grids.label: Free-air gravity
grids.note: SHGJ180U (Konopliv et al. 1999) at 6051 km, degrees 2–90 with a taper above 60. Beta, Atla and the other volcanic rises are strong highs: they are held up by hot mantle plumes.

grids.label: Geoid
grids.note: Geoid height from SHGJ180U degrees 2–180. Highs over Atla and Beta Regio, about 100 m.

shadeNote: Relief shading from a normal map that Celestia derived from the USGS Magellan altimetry DEM.

images.label: Surface map
images.note: Celestia surface texture (FarGetaNik, after John Van Vliet), shaded from Magellan data. The colours are not what the eye would see.

sites.name: Venera 4
sites.note: First probe to send data from inside another planet’s atmosphere; crushed before reaching the ground.

sites.name: Venera 5
sites.note: Atmospheric probe; stopped transmitting during descent.

sites.name: Venera 6
sites.note: Atmospheric probe; stopped transmitting during descent.

sites.name: Venera 7
sites.note: First signal from the surface of another planet (23 minutes).

sites.name: Venera 8
sites.note: Measured surface light and soil composition; 50 minutes on the surface.

sites.name: Venera 9
sites.note: First pictures from the surface of another planet.

sites.name: Venera 10
sites.note: Images and soil density of a basalt plain.

sites.name: Venera 11
sites.note: Lander; camera covers did not open.

sites.name: Venera 13
sites.note: First colour pictures and drilled soil analysis; 127 minutes.

sites.name: Venera 14
sites.note: Twin of Venera 13; landed on tholeiitic basalt.

sites.name: Vega 1 lander
sites.note: Lander; also dropped the first balloon on another planet.

sites.name: Pioneer Venus Large Probe
sites.note: Atmospheric probe; reached the surface without landing gear.

sites.name: Pioneer Venus Day Probe
sites.note: Survived the impact and transmitted from the surface for 67 minutes.

sources: Konopliv, Banerdt & Sjogren (1999), SHGJ180U gravity, Icarus 139 (copy in tudat-resources)
